doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Armstrong, the boats and the downtown halls
title: Jimmy Noon's start at the Cut-Off and the Stanton plantation
summary: Jimmy Noon started on clarinet near Stanton plantation, playing with Sam Ross and Sam Bo, and his family moved across the river after the plantation was sold. Russell knew him in Chicago but little of his early life.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Of course, a lot of them fellas didn't know them fellas back up in there. No, that's right. Like, now Jimmy Noon, now he started down there with Sam Ross and Churro, Sam Bo. Sam Bo, yeah. Used to play trombone there. That's where he started.
Was that down the coast too? Yeah, yeah. That's at the Cut-Off. At the Cut-Off, yeah. Where did Jimmy Noon come from?
That's where he come from. Stanton. Stanton. But now after Stanton sold the plantation out, Jimmy Noon moved across the river. His family moved across the river.
So where was Stanton? On this side?
Stanton on the other side, down below.
Down below. Do you know anything about Jimmy Noon's family? If his folks played anything or anybody else? Any brothers or?
I was just, he didn't know no older than me.

Yeah. Not there. I knew him in Chicago, but I never talked to him very much and never got much about his life. Yeah. I knew he came from here, but I didn't know it was on the other side even. Yes, on the other side. Yeah, on the other side.
But he started Jimmy Noon just a little before me.
Yeah. And I came up with, after that, Jimmy Noon and Frank Ross. Ross. Sam Ross. Sam Ross. Sam Ross. Sam Ross. Yeah. He was one-eyed. One-eyed. What did he play? Trumpet.

Did Jimmy Noon start on clarinet, do you think, or did he play anything else first? No, he always played clarinet. Always played clarinet. Always played clarinet. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Always played clarinet.
